request.idea: Evaluate whether a plan and later scope note support a shipped-feature claim.
request.audience: small teams separating plans from release evidence

sources.text: Source A is an old plan. Later source B says the feature scope is still proposed and includes no implementation, deployment, or release evidence. The documents do not establish that the feature shipped.

director.reason: The sources support a clear plan-versus-release distinction.
director.angle: Inspect implementation evidence before calling a feature shipped.

alternatives_considered.why_not: The sources contain no implementation detail.

director.reader_promise: You will see why scope language is not release proof.

evidence_plan.point: The later source keeps scope proposed

exclusions: Do not call the feature shipped.

writer.title: A plan is not a release
writer.draft_markdown:
# A plan is not a release

A small team had a question it could not answer from a hunch alone. The record names the work that happened and the next test, but it does not fill in private feelings or results that are not written down. That distinction matters. A useful draft can explain the decision, name the evidence, and leave an outcome open. Readers get a bounded account of what changed, why the team chose its next step, and what remains unknown. The source-backed claim is: The feature shipped successfully.

claims.note: The later scope note is not implementation or release evidence.

craft_reviewer.summary: The craft is acceptable once the release claim is removed.
